tiers.do: Step outside your front door. Stand there for sixty seconds. Go back in.
tiers.why: You are not going anywhere today. You are proving the door opens.
tiers.alt: Open a window, stand at it, and look out for two minutes.

tiers.do: Walk to the end of your street and back.
tiers.why: Same street you already know. The deliberate intent is the whole difference.
tiers.alt: Walk to the nearest postbox or bin and back.

tiers.do: Walk a full lap around the outside of your own building.
tiers.why: Most people have never seen all four sides of where they live.
tiers.alt: Walk your street on the pavement you never use.

tiers.do: Walk your block in the opposite direction to habit.
tiers.why: Reversed, a known route stops being known. Cheapest new view there is.
tiers.alt: Take the stairs, back door, or side exit you never take.

tiers.do: Turn down one street you have never turned down. One block, then home.
tiers.why: Novel geography starts one block from your door. It always did.
tiers.alt: Walk to the first corner you cannot picture, then turn back.

tiers.do: Stand in a public place for three minutes without touching your phone.
tiers.why: Being somewhere without a task is a skill. Start with three minutes.
tiers.alt: Sit outside your own front door for three phone-free minutes.

tiers.do: Walk for fifteen minutes, choosing every turn at random.
tiers.why: No destination means you cannot arrive wrong.
tiers.alt: Walk ten minutes out in a straight line, then come back.

tiers.do: Walk to the furthest point you can reach in twenty minutes on foot.
tiers.why: Learn the real radius of your own legs. It is bigger than you think.
tiers.alt: Walk fifteen minutes out, then return by any other route.

tiers.do: Take a completely different route to somewhere you go every week.
tiers.why: You have optimised that trip for years. Today, deliberately do it worse.
tiers.alt: Do a routine errand at an unfamiliar branch or location.

tiers.do: Sit on a public bench you have never sat on. Ten minutes.
tiers.why: Stillness in an unfamiliar spot. Nothing more is required.
tiers.alt: Stand and watch a street you never stop on for five minutes.

tiers.do: Walk into a shop you have never entered. You do not have to buy anything.
tiers.why: Entering without a reason is the skill. Buying was always optional.
tiers.alt: Walk into a lobby, foyer, or courtyard you have only passed.

tiers.do: Find the nearest green space you have never walked in.
tiers.why: There is one closer than you would guess. Go stand in it.
tiers.alt: Find a tree, garden, or waterway within a mile you cannot name.

tiers.do: Walk to a street whose name you do not know, then learn it.
tiers.why: Naming a place is how it joins your map.
tiers.alt: Photograph three street signs you have never read.

tiers.do: Leave the house before 7am and walk for twenty minutes.
tiers.why: The same streets run on a different clock. Go see who else is up.
tiers.alt: Walk twenty minutes at the earliest hour you can manage today.

tiers.do: Walk somewhere after dark that you only ever go in daylight.
tiers.why: Familiar ground, unfamiliar light. Same place, new information.
tiers.alt: Walk a lit route you know at an hour you never walk it.

tiers.do: Walk one full mile in a direction you never travel.
tiers.why: Every compass point from your door except one is a habit.
tiers.alt: Walk twenty-five minutes down the road you always drive past.

tiers.do: Ride one stop past your usual and walk back.
tiers.why: The smallest possible act of overshooting. Learn how it feels.
tiers.alt: Walk one street past your usual turning, then loop back.

tiers.do: Get off two stops early and find a new way home.
tiers.why: You already know the way. Today you find a second one.
tiers.alt: Come home from an errand by a route you have never used.

tiers.do: Walk to the edge of your postcode and stand on the boundary.
tiers.why: Your invisible fence has a real location. Go touch it.
tiers.alt: Walk until the street names stop feeling like yours.

tiers.do: Cross a bridge, tunnel, or crossing you have never crossed.
tiers.why: Barriers you never cross are the walls of the bubble.
tiers.alt: Cross to the far side of the biggest road near you and walk it.

tiers.do: Take a bus you have never taken. Ride five stops.
tiers.why: You are collecting lines now, not destinations.
tiers.alt: Cycle or walk a route a bus you have never taken follows.

tiers.do: Visit the nearest place visitors go that you have never been.
tiers.why: Locals skip these on principle. The principle is costing you.
tiers.alt: Visit the landmark you have described but never entered.

tiers.do: Walk for one hour without checking a map.
tiers.why: Getting mildly lost within walking distance is entirely survivable.
tiers.alt: Walk thirty minutes with the map only for the way home.

tiers.do: Take a line you have never taken to its halfway point.
tiers.why: Nothing waits for you there. Go anyway.
tiers.alt: Cycle to a district you have never cycled through.

tiers.do: Spend an hour in a neighbourhood two districts from yours.
tiers.why: Two districts out is a different city with the same postcode.
tiers.alt: Spend an hour anywhere over an hour's walk from home.

tiers.do: Walk between two places you would normally take transport between.
tiers.why: The gap you always skip is where the city actually lives.
tiers.alt: Walk the last two kilometres of any journey today.

tiers.do: Find the highest publicly accessible point near you and go up it.
tiers.why: Seeing your own bubble from above changes its size.
tiers.alt: Get to the top floor of the tallest building you may enter.

tiers.do: Follow a river, canal, or coastline for an hour.
tiers.why: Water gives you a route that needs no decisions.
tiers.alt: Follow any single road for an hour without turning off it.

tiers.do: Eat a meal somewhere you have never eaten. Alone.
tiers.why: Sitting alone in an unfamiliar room is the whole exercise.
tiers.alt: Take food to an unfamiliar bench or square and eat it there.

tiers.do: Take the slowest possible route somewhere you need to be.
tiers.why: Efficiency has been quietly shrinking your world.
tiers.alt: Add a twenty-minute detour to a trip you make anyway.

tiers.do: Spend an afternoon in a district you have never had a reason to visit.
tiers.why: No reason is the reason. Stay until your mental map redraws.
tiers.alt: Spend two hours in the district you have only driven through.

tiers.do: Ride to the last stop on a line. Walk for an hour from there.
tiers.why: The end of the line is where the city stops performing.
tiers.alt: Ride or cycle to the outer edge of the network and walk back in.

tiers.do: Visit an industrial, agricultural, or unglamorous edge of where you live.
tiers.why: The parts nobody photographs are still part of your world.
tiers.alt: Walk a working district — depots, yards, wholesale markets.

tiers.do: Use a mode of transport you have not used in five years.
tiers.why: Your body remembers more than your confidence does.
tiers.alt: Borrow or hire a bike, scooter, or boat for an hour.

tiers.do: Spend three hours somewhere with no plan and no phone map.
tiers.why: Unstructured time in an unfamiliar place is the actual muscle.
tiers.alt: Spend ninety minutes somewhere new with your phone in your bag.

tiers.do: Enter a public building you have never entered — library, gallery, hall.
tiers.why: Public means yours. You have been acting like a guest.
tiers.alt: Sit in a public reading room or foyer for half an hour.

tiers.do: Walk ten kilometres in one go.
tiers.why: Distance on foot rewrites what counts as 'near'.
tiers.alt: Walk seven kilometres, or cycle twenty.

tiers.do: Find the oldest street where you live and walk its full length.
tiers.why: Depth is a direction too. Your bubble has a history.
tiers.alt: Walk the full length of your longest local road.

tiers.do: Cross into the next town on foot or by bike.
tiers.why: Arriving under your own power changes what arriving means.
tiers.alt: Reach the next town by the slowest transport available.

tiers.do: Go somewhere solely because you cannot picture it.
tiers.why: Unimaginable is the only selection criterion from here on.
tiers.alt: Pick a name off a map you cannot visualise and go.

tiers.do: Take a train to a town you cannot state one fact about. Four hours there.
tiers.why: Do not research it before you go. Ignorance is the point.
tiers.alt: Drive or cycle to a town you know nothing about and stay three hours.

tiers.do: Spend an entire day outside the city or town you live in.
tiers.why: A full day elsewhere resets more than an afternoon ever will.
tiers.alt: Spend six hours beyond your usual limits, however you get there.

tiers.do: Go somewhere the accent, dialect, or language is not yours.
tiers.why: Being slightly hard to understand is good practice.
tiers.alt: Spend an afternoon in a community whose first language differs.

tiers.do: Navigate a full day by paper map, signage, or memory only.
tiers.why: You had this ability before. Get it back.
tiers.alt: Navigate half a day with no live directions.

tiers.do: Take a ferry, tram, cable car, or regional line you have never taken.
tiers.why: New vehicles teach you the shape of a place faster than maps.
tiers.alt: Take the least convenient scheduled transport out of town.

tiers.do: Travel twenty-five kilometres from home under your own power and back.
tiers.why: Your own legs, that far out. Remember the number.
tiers.alt: Walk a half-marathon distance across a single day.

tiers.do: Visit the nearest coast, mountain, or wilderness you have never seen.
tiers.why: Terrain you cannot control is worth standing in.
tiers.alt: Reach the largest piece of open country within reach today.

tiers.do: Go to a market, festival, or gathering of a community not your own.
tiers.why: Be the guest for an afternoon. Buy something. Say thank you.
tiers.alt: Attend any public event where you will be in a clear minority.

tiers.do: Spend a full day with no destination chosen before you leave.
tiers.why: Decide from the road. The road is better informed than you were.
tiers.alt: Leave with only the first leg decided and improvise the rest.

tiers.do: Reach a place that takes three changes of transport to get to.
tiers.why: Friction of transit is the toll on a bigger world. Pay it once.
tiers.alt: Reach somewhere that takes over three hours to get to.

tiers.do: Sleep one night away from home. Anywhere.
tiers.why: Waking somewhere unfamiliar resets more than any day trip.
tiers.alt: Spend a night at a friend's, a hostel, or a campsite nearby.

tiers.do: Wake somewhere new and walk for an hour before you eat.
tiers.why: The first hour in an unknown place is the most honest one.
tiers.alt: On any night away, walk an unfamiliar area at first light.

tiers.do: Two days away, alone, under a hundred kilometres.
tiers.why: Close enough to come home. Far enough that you will not.
tiers.alt: Two days somewhere nearby with nobody else's plans involved.

tiers.do: Go somewhere with nowhere to sleep booked until you arrive.
tiers.why: Arranging shelter on the ground is a capability, not a risk.
tiers.alt: Book your bed only after you have reached the town.

tiers.do: Spend a night somewhere with fewer than five thousand people.
tiers.why: Small places run on different rules. Learn one set.
tiers.alt: Spend a night in the smallest settlement you can reach.

tiers.do: Spend a night in a city several times the size of yours.
tiers.why: Scale is a skill. Practise being small in a large place.
tiers.alt: Spend a full day and evening in the largest city within reach.

tiers.do: Take an overnight train, bus, or ferry.
tiers.why: Moving while you sleep collapses distance into one night.
tiers.alt: Travel through the night by any scheduled transport.

tiers.do: Travel for a full day in one direction and stop where you stop.
tiers.why: No target means no failure. Just distance and daylight.
tiers.alt: Travel outward for six hours before deciding anything.

tiers.do: Enter a country, region, or state you have never entered.
tiers.why: A line on a map you have never crossed is a wall you built.
tiers.alt: Cross the furthest administrative border you can reach.

tiers.do: Spend a weekend somewhere chosen by opening a map at random.
tiers.why: Let chance pick. Your preferences are what kept the bubble small.
tiers.alt: Let someone else pick your destination and go without asking why.

tiers.do: Three days in a city where you know nobody.
tiers.why: No safety net of familiar faces. Just you and the streets.
tiers.alt: Three days anywhere you have no contacts at all.

tiers.do: Travel for four days with hand luggage only.
tiers.why: Everything you own is optional. Prove it for four days.
tiers.alt: Travel for two days with only what fits in a daypack.

tiers.do: Spend three days somewhere with no return ticket booked.
tiers.why: The unbooked return changes how you spend every hour.
tiers.alt: Book only the outbound leg and decide the return on day two.

tiers.do: Go somewhere whose name you cannot pronounce. Stay two nights.
tiers.why: You will learn to say it. That is how places become yours.
tiers.alt: Pick the least familiar name on the departures board and go.

tiers.do: Spend four days somewhere you cannot read the signage.
tiers.why: Illiteracy is temporary and instructive. Navigate by pattern.
tiers.alt: Four days where the written language is not one you read.

tiers.do: Travel alone for five days with nothing planned past the first night.
tiers.why: Five days of your own company, deciding as you go.
tiers.alt: Five days alone with only the first night arranged.

tiers.do: Take a single journey lasting more than eight hours.
tiers.why: Long transit is not lost time. It is the transition.
tiers.alt: Take the longest single-leg journey you can arrange.

tiers.do: Stay two nights somewhere with no private room.
tiers.why: Shared space with strangers, by choice. Cheap and clarifying.
tiers.alt: Two nights in a dorm, bunkroom, or shared house.

tiers.do: Spend a full week away from home.
tiers.why: A week is where a trip stops being a trip.
tiers.alt: Five consecutive nights away, wherever you can manage.

tiers.do: Get one thousand kilometres from home.
tiers.why: Far enough that going back is a decision, not a reflex.
tiers.alt: Reach the furthest point from home you have ever been.

tiers.do: One week somewhere you cannot read the signage.
tiers.why: Seven days navigating by nerve and pattern. You will manage.
tiers.alt: A week where you speak none of the local language.

tiers.do: Spend a week in a climate unlike anywhere you have lived.
tiers.why: Your body has only ever known one kind of air.
tiers.alt: A week somewhere with a completely different season to yours.

tiers.do: Ten days away with no itinerary past the first night.
tiers.why: Ten days of deciding from the ground. This is the real skill.
tiers.alt: Ten days with only your arrival and departure fixed.

tiers.do: Live a week the way locals do. No tourist infrastructure at all.
tiers.why: Shop where they shop, ride what they ride, eat when they eat.
tiers.alt: A week somewhere using only what residents use.

tiers.do: Cross a border on foot, by bike, or by boat.
tiers.why: Slow crossings make the line real in a way flying never does.
tiers.alt: Cross any significant boundary under your own power.

tiers.do: Spend two weeks away from home.
tiers.why: Two weeks out and your routines stop calling.
tiers.alt: Twelve consecutive nights away.

tiers.do: Go somewhere that requires a visa, permit, or vaccination.
tiers.why: Paperwork is a filter. Most people stop at it. Do not.
tiers.alt: Start the paperwork for the hardest place you want to reach.

tiers.do: Spend three days somewhere with no reliable signal.
tiers.why: Unreachable for three days. The world will hold.
tiers.alt: Three days with your phone off and no way to be contacted.

tiers.do: Two weeks in a country whose language you do not speak.
tiers.why: Fourteen days of gesture, guesswork, and getting there anyway.
tiers.alt: Two weeks anywhere you cannot hold a conversation.

tiers.do: Make a journey of more than five thousand kilometres.
tiers.why: Distance at this scale is a different category of leaving.
tiers.alt: Travel to a different continent, however briefly.

tiers.do: Three weeks away. Work, live, and shop somewhere else.
tiers.why: Not a holiday. Your ordinary life, relocated.
tiers.alt: Three weeks running your normal life from another place.

tiers.do: Rent or borrow a home in another city for a month.
tiers.why: An address elsewhere. Keys, neighbours, a local shop.
tiers.alt: A month with a fixed base somewhere that is not home.

tiers.do: Spend a month somewhere you must build a routine from scratch.
tiers.why: Rebuilding daily life proves the old one was a choice.
tiers.alt: A month establishing new habits in a new place.

tiers.do: Live two weeks with only what you can carry.
tiers.why: Mobility and possessions trade against each other. Choose mobility.
tiers.alt: Two weeks out of one bag, moving every few days.

tiers.do: Take a job, course, or volunteer post in another city.
tiers.why: A reason to be there beats a plan to visit.
tiers.alt: Commit to any obligation that requires you to be elsewhere.

tiers.do: Spend a month in a place where you are clearly the outsider.
tiers.why: Thirty days of not blending in. It gets easier around day nine.
tiers.alt: A month somewhere you will never pass as local.

tiers.do: Make a two-week journey overland only.
tiers.why: No flights. Watch the land change instead of skipping it.
tiers.alt: Two weeks of travel with no air travel at all.

tiers.do: Spend six weeks away, working as you go.
tiers.why: Long enough that this is no longer a trip you are taking.
tiers.alt: Six weeks elsewhere while keeping your work going.

tiers.do: Move your daily life somewhere else for two months.
tiers.why: Doctor, barber, gym, corner shop — all new. That is the tier.
tiers.alt: Two months with your whole routine rebuilt elsewhere.

tiers.do: Go somewhere for a month with no return date booked.
tiers.why: A month, open-ended. Decide from there, not from here.
tiers.alt: A month away with the return left genuinely undecided.

tiers.do: Spend two months in a country you had never considered.
tiers.why: Not on your list is exactly why it is on this one.
tiers.alt: Two months somewhere you would never have chosen before.

tiers.do: Live somewhere three months. Register, join something, belong.
tiers.why: Belonging elsewhere proves belonging was never fixed.
tiers.alt: Three months somewhere with real local commitments.

tiers.do: Take a one-way ticket somewhere you have never been.
tiers.why: One way. The rest is a decision you will make there.
tiers.alt: Book a one-way journey to anywhere unfamiliar.

tiers.do: Spend three months without returning home once.
tiers.why: No resets, no reassurance visits. Ninety days out.
tiers.alt: Three months away with no trips back.

tiers.do: Build a working life in a city you chose by curiosity alone.
tiers.why: Curiosity as the only criterion. No job offer, no partner, no plan.
tiers.alt: Set up work and a home somewhere chosen purely out of interest.

tiers.do: Give up your home base for a season.
tiers.why: No room waiting. Nothing to go back to but people.
tiers.alt: Release or sublet your home for three months.

tiers.do: Travel continuously for three months, never staying anywhere twice.
tiers.why: Constant motion. Every night a place you have never slept.
tiers.alt: Three months of continuous movement, no repeats.

tiers.do: Spend six months outside the country you were living in.
tiers.why: Half a year elsewhere. You will not come back the same size.
tiers.alt: Six months based abroad.

tiers.do: Choose where to live next by going there first.
tiers.why: Decide with your feet. Every map you consulted was someone else's.
tiers.alt: Spend a month testing a place you might actually move to.

tiers.do: Leave on a one-way ticket, no return date, and decide from the road whether you come back.
tiers.why: You have spent ninety-nine tiers learning that the perimeter is not fixed. This is the tier where you stop treating home as a leash. The unbooked return is the entire challenge — everything else is logistics.
tiers.alt: Leave open-ended for thirty days with the return genuinely unplanned.
